title: Complex Direction Sense
tagline: Year 2 — Multi-turn paths, diagonal directions, bearings and relative positions

introduction.overview: Complex direction questions use paths with many turns, turns through angles other than 90°, diagonal directions (North-east, South-west), shadows and the relative positions of several people or places. The method of Year 1 still works: keep running totals of East–West and North–South displacement, track the direction faced after each turn, and finish with Pythagoras and the compass direction.
introduction.placementRelevance: Direction sense questions with several turns and diagonal directions are commonly asked in company reasoning rounds.
introduction.realWorldContext: Navigation, drone flight plans, surveying and delivery routing use these same displacement calculations.

learningObjectives: Track the facing direction through several turns, including 45° and 135° turns
Compute net displacement and the straight-line distance
Find the compass direction of the final point from the start
Handle relative positions of several points
Use shadow facts in turning problems

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Eight directions in clockwise order: N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW (45° apart). Right turn = clockwise, left turn = anticlockwise. Common triples: 3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17, 7-24-25.

coreDefinitions: Bearing: direction measured clockwise from North (N = 0°, E = 90°, S = 180°, W = 270°).
Displacement: straight-line distance and direction from the start to the end.
Intermediate directions: NE (45°), SE (135°), SW (225°), NW (315°).
Relative position: the direction of one point as seen from another.
Shadow: falls opposite to the sun (west in the morning, east in the evening).
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: Everything reduces to coordinates. Treat East as +x and North as +y. Each leg adds to x or y. After all legs, the straight-line distance is √(x² + y²) and the direction comes from the signs of x and y.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Write the facing direction as a bearing and add the turn angle (clockwise positive). After each leg, update x and y. Use a quick sketch with North at the top.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Turning
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: New bearing = old bearing ± turn angle (right +, left −)

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Displacement
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: x = East − West;  y = North − South

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Direction from the start
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Signs of (x, y) decide the quadrant

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Relative position of two points
importantRulesAndFormulas.description: Direction from the first to the second.

mainNarrative: Draw the path with North at the top. After each leg, write the facing direction. A man facing North who walks 10 m, turns right and walks 5 m, then turns right again and walks 10 m, is now 5 m East of his start (facing South).

For 45° and 135° turns, use bearings. North-east is 45°, and a 90° clockwise turn from it gives 135° (South-east). A further 180° gives 315° (North-west), and a 45° anticlockwise turn from there gives 270° (West).
For displacement, add the legs on each axis. A walk of 3 km North, 5 km East, then 9 km North ends at (5, 12), so the distance is √(25 + 144) = 13 km and the direction is North-east.
For relative positions, set one point as the origin. If A is 5 m east of B and C is 5 m north of A, then C is at (5, 5) from B, so C is North-east of B.

For shadow questions, the shadow falls opposite to the sun. In the morning the sun is in the east, so a boy facing the sun faces East. If he turns left he faces North, and his shadow, which falls to the West, is on his left.

deepDiveAspects.title: Distance walked vs displacement
deepDiveAspects.content: The path of a walker may be long, but the displacement is the straight-line distance. Read the question carefully for which one is asked.

deepDiveAspects.title: Opposite directions in coordinates
deepDiveAspects.content: A move of 10 m West followed by 10 m East cancels. Use cancellation to shorten sums.

solvedExamples.title: Multi-leg path
solvedExamples.question: A man walks 3 km North, then 5 km East, then 9 km North. How far is he from the start and in which direction?

solvedExamples.title: Turns with relative directions
solvedExamples.question: Facing North, a man walks 10 km, turns right and walks 5 km, then turns right again and walks 10 km. How far is he from the start and in which direction?
solvedExamples.commonTrap: Assuming he returns to the start.

solvedExamples.title: Turns through 45°
solvedExamples.question: A person facing North-east turns 90° clockwise, then 180° and then 45° anticlockwise. Which direction does he face now?
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: Each turn changes the bearing by its angle.
solvedExamples.commonTrap: Turning the wrong way for anticlockwise.

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Convert directions to bearings and legs to (x, y) additions. Use triples for distances.

commonMistakes.howToAvoid: Write the facing direction after every turn.

commonMistakes.whyItHappens: Treating NE as N or E.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Eliminate options in the wrong quadrant.

easy.question: A man walks 6 km North and then 8 km East. How far is he from the start, and in which direction?
easy.explanation: Net position (x East, y North) = (8, 6). Distance = 10 km, direction North-east. The answer is 10 km North-east.

easy.question: A man walks 12 km East and then 5 km South. How far is he from the start, and in which direction?
easy.explanation: Net position (x East, y North) = (12, -5). Distance = 13 km, direction South-east. The answer is 13 km South-east.

easy.question: A man walks 15 km West and then 20 km North. How far is he from the start, and in which direction?
easy.explanation: Net position (x East, y North) = (-15, 20). Distance = 25 km, direction North-west. The answer is 25 km North-west.

intermediate.question: A man faces North, walks 10 km, turns right and walks 5 km, then turns right and walks 10 km. How far is he from the start, and in which direction?
intermediate.explanation: Net position (x East, y North) = (5, 0). Distance = 5 km, direction East. The answer is 5 km East.

intermediate.question: A man faces East, walks 6 km, turns left and walks 8 km. How far is he from the start, and in which direction?
intermediate.explanation: Net position (x East, y North) = (6, 8). Distance = 10 km, direction North-east. The answer is 10 km North-east.

intermediate.question: A man faces North, walks 20 km, turns left and walks 15 km, turns left and walks 20 km, then turns left and walks 5 km. How far is he from the start, and in which direction?
intermediate.explanation: Net position (x East, y North) = (-10, 0). Distance = 10 km, direction West. The answer is 10 km West.

advanced.question: A man walks 3 km North, then 5 km East, then 9 km North. How far is he from the start, and in which direction?
advanced.explanation: Net position (x East, y North) = (5, 12). Distance = 13 km, direction North-east. The answer is 13 km North-east.
